title: Sensorize per-tenant queue-depth + trace enrichment to detect silent capacity regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:

After the 2026-02-26 capacity incident where several tenants experienced sustained tail latency without clear error spikes, the postmortem identified two blind spots: (1) ingestion pipeline dropped per-tenant queue-depth metrics during protobuf schema rollout, and (2) key-value (KV) eviction/peek paths had inconsistent tracepoints causing silent backpressure to be invisible in console traces. This ticket tracks the cross-team remediation: add robust per-tenant queue-depth metrics, enrich traces with per-request tenant and queue context, and wire those signals into dashboards and alerts so regressions are detectable before customer impact amplifies.

Root cause (short):
- Rolling protobuf change removed a low-volume field used by the metrics bridge; the bridge silently accepted messages without emitting tenant keys during the schema mismatch window.
- Tracing hooks in the KV runtime do not propagate queue identifiers into sampled spans for cold-path evictions, so correlating latency with queue pressure required expensive ad-hoc diagnostics.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Every request touching the ingress pipeline emits a stable "queue_depth_v2" metric tagged by tenant_id and route within 99.9% of cases.
- Traces include a standardized span attribute "tenant.queue_id" for all queue enqueue/dequeue/eviction events.
- New Grafana dashboard panels: per-tenant 99th latency vs queue_depth, aggregated queue saturation heatmap, and an automated synthetic-tenant alert rule (P99 queue_depth > threshold for 3m).
- Runbook updated with playbook steps for throttling vs. shedding and automatic fallback to legacy metrics bridge.

Planned actions (this ticket):
1) Implement defensive decoding in metrics bridge to fallback to legacy tenant field when new schema field missing (runtime change).
2) Add explicit queue_depth instrumentation at ingress and at per-tenant enqueue points (metrics + delta log event).
3) Add span enrichment in runtime: propagate tenant and queue_id through async workers, ensure sampling preserves these attributes at least for one span upstream.
4) Pipeline enrichment: tag existing ingestion telemetry to avoid backfilling gaps, and add an ETL job to reconcile missing tenant tags for 48h window.
5) Dashboard & alerting: create panels and an actionable alert with runbook links; add a chaos test to exercise alerts.

Progress / current state:
- Defensive decoding PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-metrics/pull/6182 (rolled to staging 2026-03-03).
- Initial instrumentation prototype for queue_depth merged to internal branch; waiting on trace attribute propagation API review.
- Grafana dashboard skeleton created: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/console/kv-queue-insights
- Confluence postmortem and design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Silent+Capacity+Regression+2026-02-26

Decisions / trade-offs made so far:
- We will prefer metric tagging over higher-cardinality traces for long-term alerting. Traces will include identifiers but dashboards/alerts rely on metrics to avoid cardinality blowup.
- For short-term mitigation, we add a dimensionality cap to queue_depth (top-k tenants) and a sampling strategy for trace enrichment to keep storage cost bounded.

Review feedback and approvals:
- Security review requested for tenant_id propagation; privacy team confirmed tenant IDs are allowed in telemetry within internal consoles under console-2026.03 policy.
- Observability team requested we include a fallback to legacy metrics bridge (implemented in PR 6182).

Open risks and follow-ups:
- The ETL reconciliation might not fully reconstruct tenant tags for messages older than 7 days; add a telemetry indicator for coverage.
- Need to coordinate with Dedicated infra team for rollout window to avoid double-counting metrics during canary.

Next steps (owner assignment):
- Marcus Li: finalize trace enrichment API review and land propagation change (ETA 2026-03-12).
- Observability SRE (Kavita Rao): finalize dashboard panels and create alert rules (ETA 2026-03-15).
- Data platform (Ben Ortiz): implement ETL reconciliation job and provide coverage report (ETA 2026-03-18).
